items.stem: What is the fundamental scientific requirement for mechanical work to be done on an object by an applied force?

options.label: A
options.text: The object must be stationary while the heavy force is applied.

options.label: B
options.text: The object must gain excessive mass during the force application.

options.label: C
options.text: The object must be displaced along the direction of the applied force.

options.label: D
options.text: The object must be displaced completely perpendicular to the applied force.

items.answer: Work is scientifically defined as the product of the force applied to an object and its displacement in the direction of that force. If an object does not move despite heavy force, the displacement is zero, resulting in zero work. This fundamental physics concept clearly differentiates everyday effort from actual mechanical work performed on physical objects.

items.stem: A student applies a massive push force against a solid, unmoving brick wall for several minutes until physically exhausted. How much scientific work is done on the wall?

options.label: A
options.text: Positive work, because significant muscular effort was continuously exerted.

options.label: B
options.text: Negative work, because the wall pushed back with an equal opposite force.

options.label: C
options.text: Infinite work, because the wall is highly resistant to any motion.

options.label: D
options.text: Zero work, because the wall did not physically displace from its position.

items.answer: When a person pushes a rigid wall, they apply a substantial muscular force, but the wall does not move. Because the scientific definition of work strictly requires displacement in the direction of the applied force, the work done on the wall is exactly zero. The person feels tired merely due to internal muscle energy expenditure.
items.concept: Zero work when there is no displacement

items.stem: A girl walks horizontally at a constant speed while carrying a heavy box, as represented by the arrows for force (F) and displacement (s). What is the mathematical work done by the upward force applied on the box?

options.label: A
options.text: Maximum positive work, as the heavy box requires significant effort to hold.

options.label: B
options.text: Negative work, as the gravitational pull acts in the downward direction.

options.label: C
options.text: Zero work, as the applied force and the displacement are perpendicular.

options.label: D
options.text: Positive work, as she successfully moves the box in the forward direction.

items.answer: Work done by a force evaluates to zero when the applied force acts perpendicularly to the direction of displacement. Here, the girl exerts an upward force to balance the weight of the box, but the displacement is strictly horizontal. Since these two vectors form a ninety-degree angle, the resulting work done by the upward force is zero.

items.stem: During a fast-paced football match, a goalkeeper stops a fiercely kicked ball by applying force using their hands. What type of work is done by the goalkeeper on the football?
items.answer: Negative work occurs when the applied force and the displacement of the object are in directly opposite directions. When a goalkeeper catches a moving football, they apply a braking force against the ball’s motion. The ball displaces slightly backwards, opposite to the stopping force, thus resulting in negative work being done by the goalkeeper’s hands.

items.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the concept of work in physics: 1. Pushing a wheelchair forward on a flat road constitutes positive work. 2. The SI unit of work done is the newton. 3. Work done is zero if displacement is zero, regardless of applied force. Select the correct combination of statements:
items.answer: The concept of work firmly establishes that force and displacement must have a component in the same line. If displacement is zero, work is inherently zero. Pushing a wheelchair forward is a classic example of positive work because the applied muscular force aligns exactly with the forward displacement of the wheelchair on the flat ground.

items.assertion: When a person slowly carries a heavy box while walking horizontally at a constant speed, the work done by the upward carrying force is strictly zero.
items.reason: The upward force applied on the box is entirely perpendicular to the horizontal displacement of the person walking.
items.stem: Assertion (A): When a person slowly carries a heavy box while walking horizontally at a constant speed, the work done by the upward carrying force is strictly zero. Reason (R): The upward force applied on the box is entirely perpendicular to the horizontal displacement of the person walking.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false but R is true

items.answer: Work done is precisely the product of force and displacement along the direction of force. When an object moves horizontally while gravity acts vertically downwards, the angle between the gravitational force and displacement is exactly perpendicular. Consequently, there is absolutely no displacement in the direction of gravity, making the work done by gravity zero.
items.concept: Specifying force and object in work

items.stem: Two identical heavy loads are pushed up two different inclined planes to the identical vertical height h. How does the mechanical advantage of Ramp 2 mathematically compare to the mechanical advantage of Ramp 1?

options.label: A
options.text: Ramp 2 has a greater mechanical advantage because the effort force required is smaller.

options.label: B
options.text: Ramp 2 has a smaller mechanical advantage because the total distance travelled is greater.

options.label: C
options.text: Both ramps have the same mechanical advantage since the vertical height reached is identical.

options.label: D
options.text: Both ramps have a mechanical advantage of exactly one since the load mass is unchanged.

items.answer: The mechanical advantage of an inclined plane is defined as the ratio of its length to its vertical height. Since Ramp 2 possesses a greater length for the identical height, its mechanical advantage is proportionally larger. Consequently, a smaller effort force is required to move the identical load up the longer incline compared to Ramp 1.

items.stem: How is the total work done by a precisely constant force graphically determined from a standard mathematical force-displacement plot?

options.label: A
options.text: By calculating the simple slope of the plotted force line.

options.label: B
options.text: By finding the geometric area directly under the force-displacement graph.

options.label: C
options.text: By multiplying the graph’s vertical intercept precisely by its horizontal intercept.

options.label: D
options.text: By simply taking the exact square root of the force values.

items.answer: The force-displacement graph visually represents work done. For a constant force, the graph is a horizontal straight line. The area bounded by this line, the x-axis, and the initial and final position verticals forms a rectangle. Calculating this precise rectangular area mathematically directly yields the total work done on the object by the applied force.

items.stem: Match the various physical scenarios in List-I precisely with their corresponding dominant energy transformations described in List-II. List-I (Scenario): P. A glowing electric light bulb; Q. A ringing school bell; R. An operating solar cell panel; S. Food fuelling human muscle motion. List-II (Energy Transformation): 1. Chemical energy strictly into mechanical energy; 2. Light energy strictly into electrical energy; 3. Electrical energy strictly into light energy; 4. Mechanical energy strictly into sound energy. Select the correct matching sequence:
items.answer: Different scenarios exhibit various forms of energy transformation. A glowing electric bulb fundamentally converts electrical energy into light energy. Photosynthesis in green leaves involves converting solar light energy into stored chemical energy. A ringing bell transforms mechanical energy into sound energy, demonstrating how energy changes forms based on the device or natural biological process involved.

items.stem: According to the work-energy theorem, the total mechanical work effectively done on a given physical object is strictly equal to what physical parameter?

options.label: A
options.text: The exact change in its internal thermal temperature.

options.label: B
options.text: The precise change in its structural mass.

options.label: C
options.text: The total change in its kinetic or potential energy.

options.label: D
options.text: The strict inverse of its continuous moving velocity.

items.answer: The work-energy theorem fundamentally states that the net work done on an object by all applied forces exactly equals the change in its energy. Whether a force accelerates a stationary car or lifts a heavy pot against gravity, the total mechanical work effectively translates into equivalent gains in kinetic or gravitational potential energy respectively.

items.stem: A solid sphere is dropped from a certain height and falls freely under the influence of gravity. The energy values at three different positions during its fall are recorded. What are the correct numerical values for P and Q in the table? Position A (highest point): potential energy 200 J, kinetic energy 0 J, total mechanical energy 200 J; Position B (midway point): potential energy 120 J, kinetic energy P, total mechanical energy 200 J; Position C (just before impact): potential energy 0 J, kinetic energy 200 J, total mechanical energy Q.
items.answer: According to the fundamental law of conservation of mechanical energy, the total mechanical energy of a freely falling object remains completely constant. Since the total energy is 200 J at position A, it remains 200 J everywhere. Therefore, Q is 200 J. At position B, kinetic energy P equals total energy minus potential energy, yielding 80 J.
items.concept: Mechanical energy conserved in free fall

items.stem: What is the mathematically correct standard formula precisely defining the kinetic energy possessed by a structurally solid object of mass m uniformly moving with continuous velocity v?
items.answer: Kinetic energy represents the energy possessed by an object strictly due to its motion. The standard mathematical expression for calculating kinetic energy is one-half multiplied by the mass and the square of the velocity. Because mass is positive and velocity is squared, the kinetic energy of any moving physical object can never be a negative value.

items.stem: The given graph illustrates a variable force acting on a block along its direction of motion. If the block starts from rest at the origin, what physical quantity represents its kinetic energy after it has been displaced by four metres?

options.label: A
options.text: The steep slope of the line calculated from zero to two metres.

options.label: B
options.text: The maximum value of the force applied at exactly two metres.

options.label: C
options.text: The total area under the force-displacement curve up to four metres.

options.label: D
options.text: The product of the maximum force and total horizontal displacement.

items.answer: According to the work-energy theorem, the work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy. For a force-displacement graph, the total work done is calculated by finding the area under the curve. Therefore, the total area bounded by the graph and the horizontal axis directly represents the kinetic energy gained by the moving block.
items.concept: Theorem applies to systems and variable forces

items.stem: If the exact magnitude of the continuous moving velocity of a moving car strictly doubles during a highway journey, how does its new kinetic energy specifically compare to its original initial value?

options.label: A
options.text: It becomes exactly half of its original value.

options.label: B
options.text: It accurately remains perfectly the same.

options.label: C
options.text: It precisely doubles directly like the velocity.

options.label: D
options.text: It rapidly becomes exactly four times larger.

items.answer: The kinetic energy of an object is directly proportional to the square of its velocity. If a vehicle’s velocity strictly doubles, the new velocity becomes twice the original. Squaring this new velocity factor results in a fourfold increase. Therefore, the new kinetic energy will mathematically be exactly four times greater than its original initial value.
items.concept: Kinetic energy varies with velocity squared

items.stem: A lever acts as a seesaw pivoted at fulcrum C, with seating positions marked A, B, D, and E. The distances AC and EC equal 2 metres, while BC and DC equal 1 metre. A child weighing 300 N sits at seat A. Where must a heavier child weighing 600 N sit to balance the lever horizontally?

options.label: A
options.text: At seat E, which is located exactly 2 metres from the central fulcrum.

options.label: B
options.text: At seat D, which is located exactly 1 metre from the central fulcrum.

options.label: C
options.text: At seat B, which is located exactly 1 metre from the central fulcrum.

options.label: D
options.text: The seesaw cannot be balanced as the second child is significantly heavier.

items.answer: For a lever to balance perfectly, the product of the load and load arm must equal the product of the effort and effort arm. The moment created by the first child is 600 Newton-metres. To counteract and balance this, the 600-Newton child must sit at a distance of one metre on the opposite side, matching seat D.

items.stem: Read the following theoretical physical statements strictly regarding the fundamental scientific concept of kinetic energy: 1. Kinetic energy can logically be a negative numerical value. 2. The standard SI measuring unit for kinetic energy is the strictly identical joule used for mechanical work. 3. An object completely at rest definitely possesses zero kinetic energy. 4. Kinetic energy precisely depends entirely on both object mass and object speed. Select the exact correct combination of perfectly valid statements:
items.answer: Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity depending entirely on mass and the square of velocity, possessing no directional vector. The SI unit for measuring kinetic energy remains the joule, exactly like work. An object at rest possesses zero velocity, hence zero kinetic energy. Unlike velocity, kinetic energy strictly remains positive or zero under all circumstances.

items.stem: Four different objects undergo a specific displacement when a constant force is applied to them. Based on the provided data, which object experiences negative work done by the applied force? Object A: force applied 10 N, displacement 5.0 m, force in the same direction as displacement; Object B: force applied 15 N, displacement 0.0 m, force in the same direction as displacement; Object C: force applied 20 N, displacement 2.0 m, force in the direction opposite to displacement; Object D: force applied 5 N, displacement 10.0 m, force perpendicular to displacement.
items.answer: Work is accurately defined as the product of force and displacement. When force acts in the direction directly opposite to displacement, the work done is negative. Object C experiences a force opposing its ongoing motion, resulting in negative work. Objects A, B, and D experience positive, zero, and zero work respectively.

items.stem: Based on the diagram depicting the forces acting on a moving block, which force or combination of forces performs zero work on the block?
items.answer: Work is calculated as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force. If a force acts perpendicular to the displacement, it does zero work. Here, both Fgravity and Fnormal act vertically, while displacement is horizontal (a 90-degree angle). Therefore, both these forces do zero work, whereas Fpush does positive work.

items.assertion: The strictly calculated kinetic energy of a constantly moving physical object can absolutely never physically be a negative numerical value.
items.reason: The standard kinetic energy formula distinctly squares the object’s moving velocity, ensuring the final resulting mathematical calculation strictly yields entirely positive numerical values.
items.stem: Assertion (A): The strictly calculated kinetic energy of a constantly moving physical object can absolutely never physically be a negative numerical value. Reason (R): The standard kinetic energy formula distinctly squares the object’s moving velocity, ensuring the final resulting mathematical calculation strictly yields entirely positive numerical values.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false but R is true

items.answer: Both the assertion and the reason are fundamentally true statements, and the reason provides the precise mathematical explanation for the assertion. Since mass is an inherently positive physical quantity and the square of any real velocity is always positive, their product in the kinetic energy formula guarantees that kinetic energy can never be negatively valued.

items.stem: Four different water pumps lift specific loads of water to designated heights. Based on the operational data recorded, which pump delivers the highest power? (Assume acceleration due to gravity, g = 10 m/s².) Machine W: mass of water lifted 50 kg, height raised 10 m, time taken 50 s; Machine X: mass 100 kg, height 5 m, time 25 s; Machine Y: mass 20 kg, height 20 m, time 10 s; Machine Z: mass 40 kg, height 10 m, time 40 s.
items.answer: Power is defined as the exact rate of doing work, calculated by dividing the total work done by the time taken. Machine Y successfully completes 4000 J of work in merely 10 seconds, yielding a power of 400 W. This is significantly greater than the maximum power outputs of machines W, X, and Z.

items.stem: When a trained archer smoothly pulls backward on a traditional archery bowstring, what specific physical form of energy strictly accumulates directly inside the effectively deformed wooden bow?
items.answer: Elastic potential energy is accumulated strictly when an object undergoes a temporary physical deformation, such as stretching, compressing, or bending. When an archer pulls a bowstring, muscular work is done against the bow’s internal elastic forces. This applied mechanical work is effectively stored within the fundamentally deformed bow as highly usable elastic potential energy.

items.stem: A worker needs to push a heavy wooden crate up into a moving truck. Four different smooth inclined planes are available. Assuming zero friction, which ramp requires the least effort force to lift the load? Ramp K: height 2.0 m, length 6.0 m; Ramp L: height 3.0 m, length 12.0 m; Ramp M: height 1.5 m, length 4.5 m; Ramp N: height 4.0 m, length 10.0 m.
items.answer: A simple machine’s mechanical advantage is essentially the ratio of load to effort. For inclined planes, it equals the ratio of length to height. Ramp L possesses the highest mechanical advantage ratio of four, meaning it provides the greatest force multiplication. Consequently, it consistently requires the least effort to safely move a specific heavy load.

items.stem: Which precise formula mathematically calculates the exact total gravitational potential energy strictly gained by an object of mass m carefully lifted perfectly vertically to a definite height h from the ground?
items.answer: The gravitational potential energy of an object is strictly defined relative to a reference level, usually the ground. To lift an object of mass m to height h, a minimum upward force equal to its weight mg is required. The mechanical work done against gravity is mgh, which precisely becomes the stored gravitational potential energy.

items.stem: An oscillating simple pendulum moves between extreme points P and R, passing through the lowest point Q. Assuming no air resistance, which statement accurately describes the mechanical energy of the pendulum bob during its motion?

options.label: A
options.text: The kinetic energy is maximum at P and R, while potential energy is maximum at Q.

options.label: B
options.text: The total mechanical energy continually decreases as the bob moves from P to Q.

options.label: C
options.text: The potential energy at P transforms entirely into kinetic energy when reaching Q.

options.label: D
options.text: The mechanical energy is highest at P and lowest at Q due to gravitational pull.

items.answer: In the absence of external resistive forces, the total mechanical energy of a pendulum remains conserved. At the extreme point P, the bob possesses maximum potential energy and zero kinetic energy. As it descends to the lowest point Q, this potential energy converts entirely into kinetic energy, maintaining a constant total mechanical energy throughout the motion.

items.stem: A physically heavy metal block possessing exactly 10 kg of mass is slowly lifted directly upwards exactly 5 m above the floor. Strictly assuming (g = 10 m/s²), what is its newly acquired gravitational potential energy?
items.answer: Gravitational potential energy strictly depends on mass, gravitational acceleration, and vertical height. By applying the standard physics formula for potential energy (U = mgh), we multiply the mass of 10 kg, gravity of 10 m/s², and the vertical height of 5 m. This specific mathematical multiplication yields a total stored potential energy of exactly 500 joules.

items.stem: A transportation company is testing four different prototype vehicles. Based on the mass and final velocity recorded in the testing logs, which vehicle currently possesses the maximum kinetic energy? Vehicle P: mass 1000 kg, velocity 10 m/s; Vehicle Q: mass 500 kg, velocity 20 m/s; Vehicle R: mass 2000 kg, velocity 5 m/s; Vehicle S: mass 100 kg, velocity 30 m/s.
items.answer: Kinetic energy depends directly on an object’s mass and the square of its velocity. Calculating the values using the standard formula yields 50,000 J for P, 100,000 J for Q, 25,000 J for R, and 45,000 J for S. Vehicle Q possesses the highest energy because its doubled velocity heavily increases energy.
items.concept: Kinetic energy varies with velocity squared

items.stem: Carefully review these fundamental physics statements exactly regarding strictly conservative potential energy types: 1. Stretching a metal coil spring perfectly stores distinct elastic potential energy. 2. Lifting a heavy wooden box strictly increases its total gravitational potential energy. 3. Completely separating two mutually attracting opposite magnetic poles strictly decreases their combined magnetic potential energy. Identify the strictly correct combination of these statements:
items.answer: Potential energy can be stored through structural deformations or spatial arrangements. A stretched spring stores elastic potential energy due to its forced configuration. Gravitational potential energy depends precisely on height relative to the Earth’s surface. A system involving two separated magnetic poles also clearly stores magnetic potential energy due to their specific relative spatial positions.

items.stem: According to the strict fundamental scientific principle of completely conservative mechanical energy, what exactly occurs strictly to an object steadily falling freely downwards under pure uninterrupted earthly gravity?

options.label: A
options.text: Its total combined mechanical energy steadily dissipates entirely into zero.

options.label: B
options.text: Its kinetic energy fundamentally drops strictly while potential energy steadily increases.

options.label: C
options.text: Its gravitational potential energy steadily decreases strictly while kinetic energy precisely increases.

options.label: D
options.text: Its total mechanical energy continually increases strictly due to rapid gravitational acceleration.

items.answer: According to the fundamental law of conservation of mechanical energy, if an object falls freely under only the influence of gravity, neglecting air resistance, its total mechanical energy remains perfectly constant. As it descends, its stored gravitational potential energy continuously decreases, transforming precisely and completely into increasing kinetic energy without any overall net energy loss.
items.concept: Mechanical energy conserved in free fall

items.stem: Correctly arrange the following sequential energy transformation stages specifically tracking a heavy stone dropped perfectly straight downwards from a remarkably tall vertical cliff: 1. Stone hits the sandy ground and dynamically completely halts moving. 2. Gravitational potential energy dynamically begins smoothly converting entirely into kinetic energy. 3. Stone strictly possesses maximum absolute potential energy and precisely zero moving kinetic energy. 4. Stone distinctly possesses strictly maximum moving kinetic energy exactly just before immediate ground impact. Select the precise correct chronological sequential order of events:
items.answer: A freely falling object starts from a certain height possessing maximum potential energy and zero kinetic energy. As it descends, gravitational potential energy gradually transforms into kinetic energy. Just before impacting the ground, its kinetic energy reaches a maximum while potential energy becomes zero, followed finally by impact and complete cessation of the object’s motion.

items.stem: Consider the two moving blocks shown in the diagram. What is the ratio of the kinetic energy of the block on Track 1 to the kinetic energy of the block on Track 2?
items.answer: Kinetic energy depends on mass and the square of velocity (K = ½ mv²). For the first block, kinetic energy is ½m(2v)² = 2 mv². For the second block, kinetic energy is ½(2 m)v² = mv². The ratio is 2 mv² to mv², which simplifies exactly to 2:1, making the other given ratios mathematically incorrect.

items.stem: In a standard purely oscillating simple laboratory pendulum steadily swinging freely backwards and continuously forwards, exactly at which precise structural point does it genuinely possess absolutely purely pure kinetic energy?

options.label: A
options.text: Precisely at its highest absolute extreme raised position points.

options.label: B
options.text: Precisely at its absolute lowest central mean swing position.

options.label: C
options.text: Exactly halfway cleanly between the mean and the extreme positions.

options.label: D
options.text: Strictly at both completely extreme end raised points simultaneously.

items.answer: In a steadily oscillating simple pendulum, mechanical energy cyclically shifts between forms. At the extreme swing positions, the pendulum momentarily halts, possessing maximum potential energy and absolutely zero kinetic energy. As it swings through the central mean position, its vertical height is lowest, converting its potential energy entirely into maximum kinetic energy at that specific instant.
items.concept: Mechanical energy as a form of energy

items.stem: The sphere is released from rest at Point A and rolls along the frictionless track. At which point will the sphere have the maximum kinetic energy?
items.answer: According to the law of conservation of mechanical energy, potential energy transforms into kinetic energy as an object descends. The total mechanical energy remains constant. The sphere’s kinetic energy is maximized when its gravitational potential energy is minimized, which occurs at the lowest elevation on the track. Therefore, Point B represents the maximum kinetic energy.
items.concept: Slide speed from conservation of energy

items.stem: Examine the following detailed theoretical physics statements entirely concerning the strict universal law governing strictly pure unresisted mechanical energy conservation principles: 1. Total completely pure mechanical energy is universally strictly defined perfectly as only potential energy minus kinetic energy. 2. Perfect mechanical energy genuinely strictly remains completely constant exclusively in situations lacking non-conservative forces like frictional drag. 3. A downward free falling mass strictly continuously transforms precisely all losing potential energy perfectly entirely into equal kinetic energy. 4. Total unresisted mechanical energy fundamentally always perfectly mathematically absolutely strictly always stays identically perfectly constant everywhere exactly. Select the perfectly accurate combination of perfectly valid physical statements:
items.answer: Mechanical energy conservation strictly holds true when only conservative forces, like gravity, act upon the specific system. In real-world practical scenarios, mechanical energy often slowly dissipates due to non-conservative forces like friction or air resistance. The sum of kinetic and potential energies forms mechanical energy, which precisely remains constant during ideal, frictionless, unresisted free falls.

items.stem: Assuming acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s², how does the power exerted by System X compare to the power exerted by System Y?

options.label: A
options.text: System X exerts twice the power of System Y.

options.label: B
options.text: System Y exerts twice the power of System X.

options.label: C
options.text: Both systems exert the exact same power.

options.label: D
options.text: System X exerts four times the power of System Y.

items.answer: Power is the rate of doing work, calculated as (P = mgh/t). For System X, power is (50 × 10 × 10)/25 = 200 W. For System Y, power is (40 × 10 × 10)/10 = 400 W. Therefore, System Y operates at 400 W, which is exactly twice the 200 W power of System X.

items.stem: The lever shown is in a state of perfect horizontal balance. What is the magnitude of the Effort Force required, and what is the mechanical advantage of this lever?
items.answer: For a balanced lever, Load × Load Arm = Effort × Effort Arm. Hence, 600 N × 0.5 m = Effort × 2.0 m, yielding an Effort of 150 N. Mechanical advantage is the ratio of Load to Effort (600 / 150) or Effort Arm to Load Arm (2.0 / 0.5), both of which calculate to exactly 4.

items.reason: Strictly as the heavy object steadily steadily falls downwards, its entirely continually decreasing exact potential energy perfectly mathematically exactly perfectly uniquely exactly entirely instantaneously absolutely converts exactly into pure kinetic energy.

Reason (R): Strictly as the heavy object steadily steadily falls downwards, its entirely continually decreasing exact potential energy perfectly mathematically exactly perfectly uniquely exactly entirely instantaneously absolutely converts exactly into pure kinetic energy.

items.answer: The assertion correctly states that a freely falling object maintains constant mechanical energy. The precise reason is the continuous, perfectly balanced transformation between potential and kinetic energy. Every single joule of gravitational potential energy lost during descent is instantaneously and exactly converted into a joule of kinetic energy, maintaining the overall total sum completely invariable.

items.stem: In the diagram shown below, the velocity ratio of the arrangement is
items.answer: Velocity ratio is the displacement of the effort divided by the displacement of the load, which here is 2d/d = 2. Thus (b) is correct option.

items.stem: A single fixed pulley is used because

options.label: A
options.text: it changes the direction of applied effort conveniently

items.answer: A single fixed pulley is used to lift load by changing the direction of the lifting force. Even though a single fixed pulley has no mechanical gain in that, the effort applied is greater than the load. Thus (a) is correct option.

items.stem: What is the ratio of load to effort in case of a tree house elevator shown in the diagram below?
items.answer: Tree house elevator is using single fixed pulley so ratio of load to effort is 1 : 1. Thus (b) is correct option.

items.stem: Mechanical advantage is ratio of ...............
items.answer: Mechanical advantage is the ratio of load to the effort. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: A pulley is used to lift a load of 180 kgf by applying an effort of 90 kgf in the downward direction. Calculate the work done by the effort applied on the pulley.
items.answer: Load = 180 kgf and effort = 90 kgf. Velocity ratio is the displacement of the effort divided by the displacement of the load, which the book evaluates as 180/90 = 2 J. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: A woman draws water from a well using a fixed pully. The mass of the bucket and the water together is 10 kg. The force applied by the woman is 200 N. The mechanical advantage is (Take g=10 m/s²)
items.answer: Load is the weight of the water, L = 10 × 10 N = 100 N. Effort is the force applied, E = 200 N. Now MA = Load/Effort = 100/200 = 0.5. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: Name the pulley system used in the following application of lifting scrap from a junk yard:

options.label: A
options.text: Block and tackle system of pulleys.

options.label: C
options.text: Combination of single fixed and single movable pulley.

items.answer: Crane is an example of block and tackle for greater MA. Thus (a) is correct option.

items.stem: The handle of a nutcracker is 16 cm long and a nut is placed 2 cm from its hinge. If a force of 4 kgf is applied at the end of the handle to crack it, what weight, if simply, placed on the nut will crack it ?
items.answer: Effort arm = 16 cm = 16/100 m. Effort, E = 4 kgf. Load arm = 2 cm = 2/100 m. Suppose the load is L. Then L × load arm = E × effort arm, so L × (2/100) = 4 × (16/100). L = (64/100) × (100/2) = 32 kgf. Thus (b) is correct option.

items.stem: The actual mechanical advantage of a single movable pulley is :
items.answer: The ideal mechanical advantage of a single movable pulley is 2, but friction and the weight of the pulley itself reduce it, so the actual mechanical advantage is less than 2 but more than 1. Thus (b) is correct option.

items.stem: A pulley system has a velocity ratio VR = 5. If the efficiency of the system is 80%, find its MA.
items.answer: VR = 5 and efficiency = 80%. Efficiency is MA/VR, so 80 = MA/5 and MA = (80/100) × 5 = 4. Thus (a) is correct option.

items.stem: A single fixed pulley is used because :

options.label: D
options.text: it changes the direction of applied effort

items.answer: A single fixed pulley does not reduce the effort but helps in changing the direction of effort applied. As it is far easier to apply effort in a downward direction, the single fixed pulley is widely used. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: What is the MA and VR of the machine shown in the figure below:
items.answer: The pulley used is single fixed hence MA and VR are 1. Thus (c) is correct option.
